report:
Reviewed the complete diagnostic_counts claim, all eight implementation entries and all ten associated tests. Requirements are retention of parsing/expansion/resolution/signature/body diagnostics; repeated-demand deduplication without collapsing distinct equal diagnostics; malformed-source handling as test input; exhaustive one-to-one applicable marker matching including severity and multiple same-line diagnostics; global rather than greedy assignment; independent failure before snapshots; unchanged output order.

collect unconditionally runs tracked check_crate, retaining walker diagnostics and appending SignatureDiagnostic accumulations. The walker emits parse Error/incomplete expansion diagnostics, asks local signatures/bodies and includes their results, and calls LocalUseSym::diagnostics for imports. Signature Check::report accumulates at the producing query, while SignatureDiagnostic is a Salsa accumulator: repeated demands reuse that producer's emissions rather than manually deduplicating equal snapshots. Diagnostic::report appends, the collection/render paths retain vectors, and rustc's JSON parser pushes each source diagnostic record independently; no content-based deduplication collapses distinct equal diagnostics. The new import-root audit emits one ambiguity diagnostic then continues to the next import, avoiding a second unresolved-import diagnostic for the same audited import. Captured resolver/module helpers show this is a source resolution check, not an infrastructure failure.

Parser errors are represented as Error items and the walker snapshots them. Expansion failures become incomplete-expansion source diagnostics. Rustc normal error exit is accepted only with matching error diagnostics, whereas malformed transport/unexpected exit is infrastructure failure. Compiler conditions are applied before counting; ERROR and WARN retain separate severity. Each marker's candidate list includes all eligible diagnostic indices. The augmenting-path matcher can reassign a previously chosen diagnostic, giving complete bipartite matching; all markers must match and no diagnostic may remain unassigned. Matching receives an immutable diagnostic slice and only mutates a parallel assignment vector, so rendering order is preserved. CompileTest prepares both compiler results and validates markers before calling expectations, so an equal snapshot cannot bypass count failure.

Tests: incomplete_expansion_is_a_source_diagnostic requires both a Sage marker mismatch and an explicit incomplete-expansion message for missing!(). matching_preserves_identical_diagnostics_and_output_order retains a first/second/first vector, verifies three markers succeed, two fail, and rendering order is identical. matching_snapshot_cannot_hide_missing_diagnostic requires a missing-diagnostic failure despite an empty matching rendering snapshot. overlapping_locations_require_global_matching_and_exact_counts forces reassignment (first diagnostic eligible on two lines, second only one), then checks both count mismatch directions and severity mismatch. The rustc nested macro/count test requires two markers for two real errors; the structured primary/ancestry test verifies child/label exclusion, duplicate records surviving parse, and locationless diagnostics failing exhaustiveness. invalid_source_reaches_sage snapshots a real body error. signature_diagnostics_are_retained_once uses a bad signature from two callers but expects exactly one diagnostic. unused_import_is_checked snapshots an unused unresolved import. malformed_body_is_not_silently_accepted explicitly requires Sage diagnostic-marker failure rather than treating malformed input as successful. All scenarios/expectations are visible in test bodies; helper implementations are captured by the initial whole-file inputs. No TODO/N/A entries exist.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib compile::: 38 passed, including all six associated unit tests. During the immediately preceding checking-scope review on the same unchanged implementation, executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests --test review_semantics: 14 and 8 passed, including the four associated integration tests. Those executions supplement the source inspection. No production edits or weakened tests; no requested edits.
